what_happened.line: Town Meeting defeated article 10, which would have deleted the Whalom overlay district, on a counted vote of 49 yes to 57 no.
Articles 1 and 2 passed by more than two-thirds: added state aid went to the reserve fund and school lines, and salary reserve funded the first year of the DPW contract.
Two solar articles passed: a rooftop solar power purchase agreement, unanimously, and a net metering credit agreement.
Articles 8, 9 and 15 passed unanimously: two zoning bylaw corrections and a Marshall Park boundary line agreement.
Articles 3, 4, 6 and 11 to 14 were passed over; article 16, a local match for an agricultural preservation restriction, passed unanimously.

why_it_matters: The Whalom overlay district stays in the zoning bylaw, so current rules on development in that area remain in place after the repeal was defeated.
The solar agreements change what the town pays for electricity and may bring lease payments to the town, which touches the town budget, mostly taxes, over the long term.
The agricultural restriction match comes from last year's surplus, so it adds no new cost, but the DPW contract adds a cost each year through its annual cost of living adjustment.
watch_next: Article 4 (cemetery, typographical error) is to be resubmitted at the next annual or special town meeting.

why_it_matters: The budget and enterprise votes set the town's spending for FY17, which draws on taxes, user fees and state aid, and the school line assumed extra state aid that had not yet arrived.

Article 45 bears on whether the Water District could become a town department, which could affect water service, rates and well owners outside the district, so its outcome is worth confirming from the official record.

what_happened.line: Town Meeting passed the turf field and track borrowing article by more than two-thirds, after residents objected and asked for a grass field.
The cell tower land transfer and lease authority passed by more than two-thirds, after the meeting agreed to vote it separately from the turf article.
The road repair borrowing article was taken up first and is contingent on a debt exclusion at the ballot; the minutes record the vote as not audible.
The Brooks House and TC Passios transfers to the selectmen passed, the first unanimously and the second by more than two-thirds.
A floor amendment on driveway exceptions failed, and the off-street parking standards then passed by more than two-thirds.

why_it_matters: The road and turf borrowing would be repaid through taxes, so the debt exclusion ballot question on road repairs is a vote residents will be asked to take, and it would add a yearly cost to an average single family home.
The turf and track bond is meant to be serviced partly by cell tower rental income and user payments, so how much falls on the tax bill depends on that income arriving.
The new parking, driveway and site plan rules change what property owners must meet when they build or alter a site.
watch_next: The ballot vote on the debt exclusion for local road repairs, which the road article depends on.
